title: NeedleFrame: Fleet Load Calibrator and Customer Verification Kit for Dedicated Throughput
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reproducible load calibration harness (NeedleFrame) and an associated customer verification kit to measure and guarantee dedicated capacity throughput and autoscaling behavior under realistic tenant patterns.
background: Current load tools either generate synthetic uniform traffic or replay raw customer traces at full fidelity. These approaches miss subtle behavioral fingerprints (micro-bursts, request correlation, cache warm-up patterns) that materially affect throughput, tail latency, and autoscaler decisions for Dedicated pools. Sales and CS have asked for a deterministic way to demonstrate throughput guarantees to customers and to reproduce customer-reported degradation in an internal lab.
scope: Design and implement the NeedleFrame harness that: 1) extracts compact behavioral fingerprints from production traces; 2) stitches micro-patterns into configurable scenarios; 3) supports warm-cache priming for KV/prefix caching; 4) runs controlled autoscale boundary probes; 5) outputs a customer acceptance report format. Provide a customer-facing verification kit with instructions and dashboards to validate commitments.
out_of_scope: Full trace ingestion pipeline for arbitrary PB-scale logs, long-term historical trend analysis, and building a new ML-based anomaly detector (we will integrate existing telemetry and detection services).
success_metrics: Reproducibility: same NeedleFrame scenario produces <5% variance in 95th percentile latency across 5 runs
Coverage: NeedleFrame scenarios replicate >90% of observed production percentile behaviors for three pilot customers
Customer acceptance: pilot customers sign-off using the verification kit for at least two Dedicated contract renewals
Autoscale validation: harness can reliably exercise scale-up and scale-down boundaries and produce deterministic resource-time curves
testing_plan: Fingerprint extraction: run on three representative production traces and compare micro-burst histograms to originals
Scenario synthesis: generate 10 scenarios (steady, bursty, diurnal, tail-heavy, correlated multi-tenant) and validate token throughput and KV hit-rate alignment against production baselines
Warm-cache priming: implement priming step and compare cold/warm run differences; measure KV cache warm convergence time
Autoscale boundary probes: run incremental load ramps to identify scale thresholds and verify autoscaler decisions (scaling latency, overshoot)
Customer verification test: provide step-by-step playbook for customers to run a smoke harness in a controlled window and a template acceptance report
implementation_notes: NeedleFrame components: 1) profiler (trace -> fingerprint), 2) stitcher (fingerprints -> scenario), 3) runner (distributed load agents), 4) analyzer (metric alignment and delta report).
Profiling: use existing request traces stored in telemetry (redwood-traces-prod) and sample sensitive fields; all customer PII must be redacted before processing.
Load runner: extend the existing replay framework to support correlated multi-tenancy by generating request groups with controlled interleaving and affinity tags.
Autoscale probes: implement a 'ramp with hold' protocol—linear ramp to target RPS, hold for X seconds to observe scaling, then step-down—to measure scaling hysteresis.
Determinism: scenario seeds must be exportable so customers and internal labs can reproduce runs exactly; include deterministic KV priming sequence.
Observability: the harness must emit a combined run manifest that links to Console traces, per-shard GPU utilization, token rates, and autoscaler events for side-by-side comparison.
Security: all customer demo runs must be scoped to non-sensitive datasets or synthetic prompts; provide a secure channel for customers to share verified seed manifests if needed.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Prototype profiler and stitcher; validate fingerprint representativeness on two internal services
Week 2: Implement runner extensions for correlated groups and KV priming; run lab experiments against a single Dedicated pool
Week 3: Add analyzer and templated acceptance report; run 5 repeatability experiments and tune seeds
Week 4: Pilot with two customers (sales-led); gather feedback and update playbook
Week 5: Documentation and Console integration for 'Run NeedleFrame' in Dedicated UI; prepare training for Solutions Engineers
